title: Domain property transported from a filtered colimit cocone
statement: For a filtered diagram of commutative rings, if every stage is a domain and a cocone is colimiting, then its vertex is a domain after identifying it with a specified ring.

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, Tag 037D, common-stage lifting argument

proof.text: Transport along the vertex equality. Install the domain instances at every stage. Mathlib CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.nontrivial gives nontriviality of the cocone vertex.

The forgetful functor to types preserves filtered colimits. Apply Types.FilteredColimit.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit₂ to represent the two factors a and b at one stage i. Map their product to the vertex; it is zero by the original zero-product hypothesis and preservation of multiplication.

Apply Types.FilteredColimit.isColimit_eq_iff' to the product and zero at i, obtaining a map i → j at which the product is zero. Since D(j) is a domain, one image factor is zero. Cocone naturality and preservation of zero show that the corresponding original factor is zero. This constructs NoZeroDivisors at the vertex; NoZeroDivisors.to_isDomain combines it with nontriviality.
